stations.note: Black. The first line alone, modern medicine in orange. Say it and hold.
The second half of the sentence arrives. Physically change, physically remove.
The line about 150 years sits on top and the road draws itself in. Nothing on it yet.
From opening the body. Open surgery: see it, touch it, feel it.
To small incisions. Laparoscopy: touch goes, vision stays.
To the vascular highways. This is the one everything after depends on.
One press: the dot drives itself off the last curve and we land in the room. Top view, C-arm in place. Say nothing — let it arrive.
The transportation-network line, in the room.
Her vasculature lights up across the whole body.
Enormous implications. The chart is empty — one bar per line from here.
Needle-sized access.
Recovery and trauma.
Length of stay.
Cost.
The implications clear and the line stands alone under her: one of the greatest substitution stories in medicine.
The cardiovascular uses. The four lines and their four tags arrive by themselves — let them land before you speak.
The C-arm slides out of the frame as this lands. A route to disease itself — the first column stays and the four new sites arrive on the other side, in orange.
Not only balloons and stents. Land on precisely where they are needed.
All the tags clear and one path lights the whole way up. Say the discovery line over it.
The C-arm slides away and the camera drops onto the right common femoral. This is the door.
Through the wall and into the lumen. Let the entry finish, then the tradeoff line.
As the incision disappeared, direct human perception disappeared with it. The setup steps back.
The question comes toward us down the lumen and holds. A metre away, opaque, deformable, no line of sight — say all of that over it. This is the last thing they see before the white.
Everything slides to white. All three fluoroscopy frames arrive together. Say nothing yet.
And this is what they see. Then the inference — resistance at the fingertips, and experience.
The right half: the tunnel, seen through a windscreen.
The lights go out.
The windscreen goes.
Grainy, intermittent. Hold on this one.
Clean white. Extraordinary medicine, extraordinarily difficult to scale.
One patient, one surgeon, one resident, the team around them.
Twice the operations. Everything doubles. Let them count it.
The phrase alone. Bound by a linear labor-to-output relationship.
The question, alone. Ask it and wait.
Two questions. They stay up for the whole section.
An internal representation of the world. Perception is not only vision.
Nature: the bat, and every other sensing modality evolution picked.
Engineering: the same answer, different sensors, fused.
The board goes up, with the lesson written across the top as the synthesis.
The working out underneath, arriving by itself: a decision problem, then the missing model of the world, then perception first. The bubbles arrive one at a time.
Alone. But perception had to come first. Do not rush off this one.
Mosaic. Why the vascular system first.
White slides away and we are back in the vessel where we left it. Much like AVs did, we start by — the loop is empty.
Restoring perception. Sensing at the tool–anatomy interface; the anatomical scene, understood as they move.
Generating understanding. Interactions become data; what happened, what went wrong, how they recovered.
Closing the loop on action. Dexterity and fine motion a metre away — and the loop closes.
Perception creates data. One line, alone in the vessel. Let it sit.
Data creates understanding. Bigger; the first line steps back.
Understanding enables increasingly intelligent action. The largest; the others fade behind it. This is the compounding.
Out of the vessel, back to the room, no C-arm. Surgical intelligence emerges from the bottom up.
Every embodied intelligent system.
Less invasive, then more intelligent.
The one becomes many. Once surgery can be perceived, it can be learnt.
Once it can be learnt, it can be scaled.
They resolve into the mark, slowly: the sentence goes, they gather, the mark holds orange, then the name arrives. Do not speak over it. Then thank the room.
